protein: Tgo-D4K (engineered FANA polymerase)
source_organism: Thermococcus gorgonarius
readout: FANA synthesis rate, normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent (fold)
assay_method: Polymerase kinetic profiling (PKPro). 20 nM polymerase, 1 uM 30-mer DNA template, 100 uM each NTP, 1x ThermoPol buffer, 2x LC Green Plus; denature 95 degC 3 min, extend 55 degC 30 min, fluorescence every 6 s; rate from a linear fit of nucleotides per polymerase vs time; mean of three independent replicates.
remark: No WT row: the readout is already normalized to the Tgo-D4K parent, which is 1.0 by definition. The reference sequence is the engineered Tgo-D4K parent, not native Tgo. Position 659 follows the source data, which carries Y and lists the variant as Y659E; the paper text instead calls it H659E. Q93A is listed twice with values differing by 7e-5, and the mean is used.

protein: Rma cyt c (monoheme c-type cytochrome, native electron carrier; engineered here as a carbene transferase)
source_organism: Rhodothermus marinus
readout: Product yield (%), C-B bond formation (carbene B-H insertion); plate-normalized, can exceed 100%
assay_method: Whole-cell biocatalysis, 96-well plate screen, anaerobic. E. cloni BL21(DE3) with pET-22b(+) cytochrome c variant and pEC86; induced 20 uM IPTG / 200 uM ALA, 20 degC, 22 h; cells resuspended in M9-N pH 7.4 with 5 mM NHC-BH3 and 7.5 mM ethyl 2-diazopropanoate, room temperature, 12 h. Chiral HPLC (Daicel IC, 47% i-PrOH/hexanes, 1.4 ml/min) against an authentic-product calibration curve; yields scaled per plate by the mean of 8 MMDTDT reference wells.
remark: Sequence is not from the paper: residues 2-124 are PDB 6CUK chain A (His6 tag 2-7, mature Rma cyt c 8-124 = UniProt B3FQS5 36-152); position 1, absent there, is padded with Met so the published numbering is 1-indexed. 160 wells collapse to 149 variants: 9 were picked more than once and are averaged, though the replicates disagree (worst: MLLSDA 63/108). No WT row: wild type was not screened, and the MMDTDT plate-reference wells are absent from the source tables. Enantiomeric ratio is not included; the NNK control library is excluded, its members having no genotype.

protein: RpBE (1,4-alpha-glucan branching enzyme GlgB)
source_organism: Rhodothermus profundi
readout: Relative activity (fold) of branching/total activity on amylose, relative to WT RpBE
assay_method: Iodine-staining branching-activity assay. 1.25 mg/mL potato amylose type III (from a 100 g/L DMSO stock) and purified His-tagged enzyme in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0, incubated 20 min at the enzyme's optimal temperature (60 degC for RpBE); reaction stopped by boiling 15 min and cooled, then 10 uL mixed with 150 uL iodine reagent (0.0127% w/v I2, 0.035% w/v KI) in a 96-well plate, 10 min at room temperature, absorbance read at 660 nm. One unit is the enzyme amount reducing the absorbance by 1% per minute; enzyme dosage adjusted to keep A660 within 0.2-0.8. Mean of three independent replicates.
remark: Sequence is PDB 8ZQA, the authors' own WT RpBE crystal, identical over all 620 residues to UniProt A0A1M6PD84; the pET28a N-terminal His-tag of the assayed construct is not included, as its sequence is not given. 90 source rows give 88: the wild type is printed identically in all three figure sheets and collapses to one row. Two blocks are merged: Supplementary Table 10 (47 Rosetta-designed variants, already fold) and Supplementary Figs 11, 14 and 17 (40 variants in %, divided by their measured WT of 100.73 so the wild type reads exactly 1.0 as those captions declare); the blocks share no variant, so the merge rests entirely on that control. Not included: the twelve-BE activity panel and its thermal profile (a homolog panel with no single wild-type sequence), the enzyme kinetics and product DP profiles (WT and 2 variants), the CD spectra, and all docking and MD energies (not measurements).

protein: jGCaMP7s (genetically encoded calcium indicator; cpGFP inserted between calmodulin and the M13 calmodulin-binding peptide)
source_organism: synthetic construct
readout: dF/F0 (%), peak fluorescence response to 10 uM acetylcholine, mean over ROIs
assay_method: HEK293 Gq/IP3 acetylcholine assay. HEK293 cells transfected with the pCAG-driven jGCaMP7s variant (Lipofectamine 3000); at 48 h post-transfection, imaged in Tyrode's solution on a Leica DMI8 epifluorescence microscope (Photometrics Prime95B sCMOS, 20x/0.40 NA, 474/27 ex, 520/35 em) while acetylcholine was pipetted in to 10 uM final. Cells segmented with Cellpose and per-ROI dF/F0 = (F - F0)/F0 x 100 computed by the FUSE platform, F0 being each ROI's own pre-stimulus baseline; the readout is the mean over ROIs (n = 145 to 1492 per variant).
remark: Sequence is GenBank QCW12731.1 (CDS MK749391.1), the jGCaMP7s construct deposited by Dana et al. 2019, which this paper does not print; its N-terminal His6/RSET tag is part of that CDS and the published residue numbering requires it. 26 source labels give 23 rows: WT and L317H are printed in both sheets with identical ROI values and are kept once, and L317H/G392W is excluded, having only 3 ROIs against 145 to 1492 for every other construct. Two sources are merged, Source Data Figure3B (16 single mutants) and Figure4E (7 combinatorial mutants), which agree exactly on the two genotypes they share. Supplementary Table 10, which the SI states holds the data of Figure 4E, likewise omits L317H/G392W. The GCaMP generation panel (Fig. 4g,h and Supplementary Tables 13-26) is not included, having no single wild type, and jGCaMP8f A289H is a single variant on another scaffold.

protein: ParD3 antitoxin (CopG/Arc/MetJ family; neutralizes the cognate toxin ParE3)
source_organism: Mesorhizobium opportunistum
readout: Normalized growth rate (GR): log read ratio post/pre selection, linearly scaled so truncated antitoxins read 0 and wild type reads 1
assay_method: Competitive growth selection in E. coli co-expressing wild-type toxin ParE3 (pBAD33, arabinose-induced) with the ParD3 variant library on pEXT20 (IPTG-induced); only variants that neutralize the toxin proliferate. Variant frequencies counted by paired-end high-throughput sequencing at two timepoints, reads merged with FLASH and quality-filtered with vsearch; log read ratio computed for variants with at least three reads pre- and post-selection with one pseudocount, over two biological replicates (Pearson r = 0.93). Variants with GR near 0 are not resolved by sequencing depth.
remark: Sequence is not from the paper: it is UniProt F7YBW8, identical to PDB 5CEG chain A (DBREF 1-93, no SEQADV), and the source workbook numbers the mutated sites without the initiator Met, so a +1 offset was adopted to match the paper's own Fig. 2 convention (L48, D52, I53, R55, L56, F74, R78, E80, A81, R82). Of 10658 source rows, 2620 carrying stop codons were dropped as they have no substitution genotype, and 90 duplicate genotype groups (205 rows, arising from distinct DNA variants of the same protein) were averaged, worst spread 0.797. The 18 wild-type rows average to exactly 1.000000, confirming the stated normalization anchor. Not extracted: the 2620 truncated antitoxins, the 16 CoVES-designed variants scored only by plate serial dilution in Fig. 3c, and the 3-position ParD3 library, which was previously published (ref. 11); the GB1, PABP, GRB2, AAV and GFP datasets in the source data are published benchmarks reused by this paper.

protein: Nb4OMT (norbelladine 4'-O-methyltransferase; SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase of the amaryllidaceae alkaloid pathway)
source_organism: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
readout: Relative biosensor response (RFU/OD600), as fold over wild-type Nb4OMT; reports in vivo 4'-O-methylnorbelladine titre
assay_method: Biosensor-linked methyltransferase activity assay. E. coli DH10B co-transformed with the Nb4OMT variant (P150-RBS(riboJ) on a pReg-RamR backbone, no regulator) and the evolved 4'-O-methylnorbelladine reporter plasmid pSens-4NB2; three colonies per variant were grown overnight, diluted 50-fold into 1 mL LB containing 100 uM norbelladine in a 96-deep-well plate, and grown 24 h at 37 degC. Cells were pelleted, resuspended in PBS, and GFP fluorescence (ex 485 nm, em 509 nm) and absorbance at 600 nm read on a Tecan Infinite M1000.
remark: The readout is derived: fluorescence was divided by OD600 and then by the wild-type value of its own plate run, so the wild type is 1.0 by construction rather than measured. Two source blocks recorded at this same condition (100 uM norbelladine, 37 degC) were merged after that rebasing - Supplementary Fig. 8c, the 22 single MutComputeX designs, and Fig. 5a, which adds 12 combinatorial variants whose genotypes come from Supplementary Table 3; the five variants present in both agree to within 10.2%, the worst being V203E. The EMPTY and TAA background wells were dropped as they carry no genotype. The Supplementary Fig. 8 caption states biological triplicate, but its source-data sheets carry four replicate columns; all four were averaged. Not extracted: the other five culture conditions in Supplementary Fig. 8 (100 and 1000 uM norbelladine at 23, 30 and 37 degC), which are separate work items not requested; the seven RamR biosensor variants of Fig. 2 and Supplementary Fig. 2, the two constructs with HPLC titres in Supplementary Fig. 9 and the four in the Fig. 5b time course, all below the 20-variant floor; and the FireProtDB delta-Tm and delta-delta-G sets used to validate the 3DResNet, which are previously published.

protein: TadA-8e (adenosine deaminase domain of the adenine base editor ABE8e, monomeric; evolved here by CDEM)
source_organism: Escherichia coli
readout: Percentage of total sequencing reads with the target adenine converted to G at protospacer position A5 of HEK293T genomic ABE site 3
assay_method: HEK293T cells transfected with the ABE8e-architecture base editor carrying the evolved TadA-8e variant together with an sgRNA against the indicated genomic site; genomic DNA was amplified and subjected to targeted amplicon sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 in PE150 mode. Editing efficiency was quantified with CRISPResso2 v2.0.3 in batch mode (--base_edit --wc -8) from the Quantification_window_nucleotide_percentage_table output.
remark: Sequence is not quoted directly: the ABE8e parent was reconstructed as the consensus of the six evolved deaminase sequences printed in Supplementary Sequences 1, with the residue at position 106 set to R as required by the R107G entries of Supplementary Table 2, and it reproduces all four genotypes that Supplementary Table 2 states (E2, E4, E11, E14) exactly. It spans the deaminase domain plus the C-terminal fusion linker as printed, since the S171G carried by E8 and E14 lies in that linker. The source uses two numbering conventions one apart - the columnar positions of the Supplementary Fig. 10a genotype table and Supplementary Table 2 run one higher than the same table's own 'other mutations' column - and this file adopts the lower one, which is the sequence's own 1-indexing. The readout position was chosen as the parent ABE8e's own peak position (A5), which is the peak at all four sites; the source reports one value per variant per position with no replicate columns. Variant E19 is absent from this site's block in the source, so this file carries 20 variants where the other three sites carry 21. Genotypes were recovered from the Supplementary Fig. 10a table by word-coordinate extraction, since its plain text loses the column each residue belongs to; the six variants that also have printed sequences reproduce exactly. Synonymous entries in the 'other mutations' column, written with codon notation such as R63(AGA/G), were dropped. Not extracted: the other protospacer positions at this and the other three sites, which are separate work items; the 16 ABEmax-derived variants, below the 20-variant floor and carrying mutations across both chains of a TadA/TadA* heterodimer; and the APOBEC1 cytidine deaminase series, of which only four variants were characterised.

protein: RgDAAO (D-amino acid oxidase, FAD-dependent oxidoreductase)
source_organism: Rhodotorula gracilis (Rhodotorula toruloides)
readout: Activity fitness score: log2 of the variant's weighted-mean tyramide-488 proximity-labelling signal over that of wild-type DAOx; higher means more D-amino acid oxidase activity
assay_method: Enzyme proximity sequencing (EP-Seq) on yeast displaying DAOx: H2O2 generated by DAOx turnover drives horseradish-peroxidase-mediated radical labelling of the cell wall with tyramide-488, so the fluorescent label reports catalytic activity with single-cell fidelity. Cells were sorted by FACS into four bins of increasing tyramide-488 signal and variant abundance per bin read out by Illumina UMI sequencing; the activity score was taken as the expected fluorescence across the four bins. Two biological replicates, Pearson r = 0.96 (n = 7036).
remark: The sequence is UniProt P80324, which every one of the 364 scanned positions verifies against with no offset; the assayed molecule was the Aga2 display fusion carrying an N-terminal GTPTPTPTPTGEF linker and a C-terminal tag, and only the enzyme itself is given here. The scan covers positions 2-365, so positions 1 and 366-368 carry no variant. 332 nonsense variants were dropped as a premature stop cannot be written as a substitution. This sheet carries no synonymous rows. The wild type reads exactly 0 because the score is defined as a log2 ratio against it, not because it was measured separately. Not extracted: the twelve individually cloned variants used to validate the screen, below the 20-variant floor, and the FoldX delta-delta-G values, which are computed rather than measured.

protein: MiCGT (C-glycosyltransferase, UGT1 family)
source_organism: Mangifera indica
readout: Relative C-glycosylation activity toward acceptor 1a (product 2a), as fold over wild-type MiCGT
assay_method: Whole-cell biotransformation with E. coli ROSETTA (DE3) expressing the MiCGT variant, in 2 mL reaction buffer (3 mM acceptor 1a, 100 mM potassium phosphate pH 8.0, 2% glucose) at 30 degC for 24 h, with wild-type MiCGT as the control. Reactions were centrifuged and analysed by HPLC/UV on an Agilent SB-C18 column (4.6 x 250 mm, 5 um) at 1 mL/min, 30 degC; activity was taken from the product peak area. Two independent reactions per variant.
remark: The sequence is quoted from Supplementary Methods, 'The original sequence of MiCGT'; all 21 scanned positions verify against it with no offset. The wild type reads exactly 1 because the activity is expressed as a fold over it, not because it was measured separately; the two reaction replicates were averaged. Fourteen of the 21 variants read exactly 0 in the companion O-glycosylation series but none do here; the spread runs from 0.06 to 4.51. Not extracted: the companion readout for the other glycosylation reaction on this same plate, which is its own work item; the nine SSM and ISM lineage variants of Fig. 2c and the four other glycosyltransferases of Fig. 4b, all below the 20-variant floor, the latter also lacking a shared wild type; and the substrate-scope panel of Fig. 5, which varies the acceptor rather than the protein.

protein: N559 (reconstructed ancestral imine reductase, NADPH-dependent oxidoreductase)
source_organism: ancestral reconstruction (imine reductase family; extant relatives are actinobacterial)
readout: Conversion of imine substrate 1a after a 10 h reaction (fraction of substrate converted)
assay_method: Analytical-scale reaction with purified enzyme: 500 uL containing 5 mM substrate 1a, 1 mM NADP+, 30 mM D-glucose, 2 mg/mL glucose dehydrogenase, 1 mg/mL purified variant and 100 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0, at 30 degC and 800 rpm. Reactions were quenched with 10 M NaOH, extracted into methyl tert-butyl ether, dried over magnesium sulfate and analysed by gas chromatography. Three replicate experiments per variant.
remark: The sequence is quoted from the Supplementary Information, 'Amino acid sequence of N559', with the vector-derived N-terminal tag MGSSHHHHHHSSGLVPRGSH removed; all six landscape mutations verify against it. No WT row: N559 itself is absent from the Fig. 5 landscape, and the conversion reported for it in Supplementary Table 2 comes from a different experiment, so it was not merged in. This file carries only the variants measured at 10 h. The Methods state that 15 mutants were instead reacted for 3 h, but the list as printed names only 14 distinct variants - 'N559-T94S/A119G/I120V' appears twice and one comma is missing - so a fifteenth 3 h variant exists that cannot be identified and may still be among these 48. Because the 3 h group is the fast one, this subset is biased toward the lower-activity part of the landscape. The landscape is the complete combinatorial enumeration of six substitutions (L19M, C67S, T94S, A119G, I120V, D170Y) that separate N559 from N560, minus the sextuple; N559 and N560 differ at 47 positions in total, of which only these six are varied here. Not extracted: the enantiomeric excess measured on the same plate, which is a selectivity whose preferred direction the curation did not fix; the 18 ancestral nodes of Supplementary Table 2, which are separate proteins differing at dozens of positions rather than a variant series; and the kinetics of Supplementary Table 7.

protein: GkOYE.8 (engineered old yellow enzyme, ene-reductase repurposed as a Morita-Baylis-Hillman carboligase)
source_organism: Geobacillus kaustophilus
readout: Relative yield of Morita-Baylis-Hillman adduct 3, as fold over the GkOYE.8 parent measured on the same plate
assay_method: Purified-enzyme reaction in 300 uL PBS pH 10.0 containing 5 mM substrate 1, 1 mM substrate 2, 100 uM purified variant and 3% methanol as cosolvent, incubated at 25 degC and 220 rpm for 40 h. Reactions were quenched with an equal volume of 1 M HCl, centrifuged, filtered through 0.22 um membranes and quantified by HPLC (Waters Alliance e2695, UV 269 nm, Agilent SB-C18 150 x 4.6 mm, acetonitrile:water with 0.7% acetic acid 30:70, 1 mL/min, 25 degC). Three replicates per variant.
remark: The reference is not the wild type: GkOYE.8 is the engineered parent GkOYE Q102A/Y169F/R215A/R308A, built here from the GkOYE sequence given in Supplementary Data 1, and every one of the scanned positions verifies against it. That the alanine scan calls position 169 F169A rather than Y169A is independent confirmation that this parent, not wild-type GkOYE, is the background. The sequence keeps the C-terminal Strep-tag II as printed. The wild type reads exactly 1 because each block was rebased on its own GkOYE.8 control, not because it was measured separately. Three source blocks were merged - Fig. 4e, the 17-residue alanine scan, Fig. 4f, the 19-substitution C26 saturation, and Fig. 4g, the 18-substitution H164 saturation - each first divided by its own GkOYE.8 (raw 98.32, 102.69 and 94.83 respectively). Only two genotypes are shared between blocks and they do not agree equally well: C26A differs by 6% between Fig. 4e and Fig. 4f, but H164A differs by 61% between Fig. 4e (0.269) and Fig. 4g (0.503); both overlaps were averaged, so the cross-block comparability of this file rests on weaker evidence than a single-plate dataset would. Not extracted: the GkOYE to GkOYE.8 lineage of Fig. 3 and the GkOYE.11/.12/.13 variants of Figs. 5 and 6, all below the 20-variant floor; the enantiomeric excess measured for a few variants; and the five other old yellow enzymes of Supplementary Data 1, which share no wild type with GkOYE.

protein: Salivaricin B core peptide (SboA core, the class II lanthipeptide matured by SboM dehydration/cyclization and released by SboT)
source_organism: Streptococcus salivarius (UniProt Q09II3), cell-free expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 Star (DE3) extract
readout: -delta OD600 of Staphylococcus aureus RN4220 after 12 h of co-cultivation with the peptide; higher (less negative) means stronger inhibition
assay_method: UniBioCat one-pot cell-free biosynthesis. Linear DNA templates carrying a T7 promoter, the mutated sboA gene and a T7 terminator were built by overlap PCR and expressed in chaperone-enriched, SboM-enriched cell extract from an E. coli BL21 Star (DE3) degP pepN double-deletion strain, co-expressed with SboT for leader-peptide removal. Each variant's peptide concentration was determined first (Fig. 3c, Supplementary Table 5) and equal amounts were dosed: 80 uL of each unpurified cell-free reaction (diluted as needed, roughly 6-7 uM final peptide) was mixed with 120 uL LB carrying S. aureus RN4220 at a starting OD600 of 0.02 in a 96-well plate, incubated at 37 degC and 150 rpm for 12 h with OD600 read every 2 h, and delta OD600 taken as the activity measure. Values are the mean of two independent experiments.

protein: EGFR, epidermal growth factor receptor (receptor tyrosine kinase), full-length ORF expressed from a lentiviral vector
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt P00533), screened in the EGFR-dependent PC9 lung adenocarcinoma line
readout: Z-score of the log2 fold-change in variant representation after 10 days of 200 nM erlotinib relative to the plasmid library; higher means more erlotinib-insensitive
assay_method: Pooled saturation-mutagenesis screen. PC9 cells were transduced at low MOI with a lentiviral library of about 24,000 EGFR ORF variants, puromycin-selected for 3-5 days, then treated with 200 nM erlotinib (or fresh media for the untreated arm) and passaged every 3-4 days, and harvested 10 days after the start of treatment. Genomic DNA was extracted, the integrated ORF amplified by PCR, shotgun-sheared with transposon, index-labelled by Nextera XT and sequenced on Illumina NovaSeq S4. Reads were processed with the Broad Institute's AnalyzeSaturationMutagenesis to tally per-variant counts. remark: Readout is the Z-score column of Supplementary Data 1 sheet "All", used as it stands. Sequence is UniProt P00533 (1210 aa, the precursor including the 24-residue signal peptide) fetched whole; the label check passes with bad = 0 across all 21918 missense labels, which span positions 2-1210 over 1208 distinct positions, so the paper numbers in precursor coordinates. There is no WT row and wt_readout is left empty: the Z-score is standardised across the variant population rather than anchored on a measured wild-type, and the sheet carries no wild-type entry, so normalized-score anchors on the dataset mean. Consistent with that, the readout column's own mean is -0.005 and its population standard deviation 1.011. The 616 nonsense variants of the same screen (the sheet's unlabelled rows, listed separately under "Stop Codons") cannot be written as {WT}{pos}{MUT} and are excluded, leaving 21918 of the 22534 scored variants. Not included as separate work items: Supplementary Data 2, which re-lists subsets of the same Z-scores annotated against four earlier studies and adds no measurement; the afatinib, dacomitinib, osimertinib and other TKI dose-response curves of Figs. 3-7, which are individual-variant validations of a few dozen variants rather than a scan; and the two glioblastoma patient case reports. protein: PLpro, the papain-like protease domain of SARS-CoV-2 nsp3 (viral polyprotein processing, plus de-ubiquitylating and de-ISGylating activity)
source_organism: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (UniProt P0DTD1 residues 1564-1878), expressed in HEK293T biosensor cells
readout: Normalized activity fitness score from a FRET protease biosensor; 1 = synonymous wild-type, 0 = nonsense
assay_method: Barcoded lentiviral single-site mutagenesis library of PLpro under a TetOn promoter, transduced into HEK293T cells carrying a FRET cleavage biosensor; PLpro expression induced with doxycycline and cells sorted by FACS. Barcodes from the sorted gates were sequenced on Illumina and ratiometric per-variant scores with modelled errors computed with DiMSum. Scores were normalised so that the mean of synonymous wild-type variants is 1 and nonsense variants 0, and filtered for low counts and high errors. For activity, cells were sorted on cleavage of the intracellular FRET biosensor (TLKGG-APTKV linker between mClover3/mRuby3); variants enriched in the FRET-negative gate carry active PLpro. Scores merge 7 independent transductions.
remark: Sequence is the 315-residue PLpro domain derived from the scan itself, per Phase 3f: the WT_AA column of Source Data sheet "Fig. 3" gives a single unambiguous residue at each of positions 1-315, so bad is empty by construction. The derived string is byte-identical to residues 1564-1878 of UniProt P0DTD1 (SARS-CoV-2 pp1ab), which is the canonical PLpro domain, so the check is not circular. The wild-type row is written as 1.0, the value the normalisation defines rather than a measured number. Position 0 of the source tables is the expression construct's initiator Met, outside the paper's own 1-315 numbering, and its 1 missense entry is excluded; nonsense variants and the 570 synonymous controls (which carry no position) are the normalisation anchors, not work items. Phase 7: the paper states that "no mutations were permitted at the PLpro active site (Cys111, His272, Asp286)" and that the four zinc-coordinating cysteines are likewise intolerant. In the activity file all 19 substitutions at each of those seven positions sit near 0 against a wild-type anchor of 1 - position means 0.151 (C111), 0.011 (H272), 0.027 (D286), 0.074 (C189), 0.097 (C192), 0.076 (C224), 0.045 (C226) - against a whole-library mean of 0.612, and the single best substitution anywhere among them reaches only 0.33. The other readouts of the same workbook are separate work items: activity (Fig. 2), abundance (Supplementary Fig. 4), 3k drug escape (Supplementary Fig. 6) and 5c drug escape (Supplementary Fig. 7). The combined 3k-and-5c map (Supplementary Fig. 9, identical to the fitness_drug and fitness_3K columns of sheet "Fig. 4", which agree to 0.0) is a merge of the two per-drug scans and is not shipped separately. Not included: the leaky-expression profile (Supplementary Fig. 11), which measures how poorly a variant's doxycycline control holds rather than a property of the protein; and the recombinant-enzyme kinetics and dose-response curves of Figs. 1, 4 and 5, which cover a handful of variants.

readout: T-to-G editing activity as a fold change over the gTBEv0.3 parent measured on the same plate; higher is more active
assay_method: Fluorescent reporter assay in HEK293T cells. The editor (nCas9 nickase fused at its N-terminus to the engineered UNG2delta88 moiety) was co-transfected with a target sgRNA and a T-to-G reporter in which the intended base conversion restores EGFP; BFP marks transfected cells and the readout is the percentage of EGFP+ among BFP+ cells, measured by flow cytometry over 3 independent biological replicates.
remark: Sequence is UNG2delta88, residues 89-313 of UniProt P13051 (human uracil-DNA glycosylase, UNG2 isoform), with the parent substitution Y156A applied. The paper numbers every mutation in full-length UNG2 coordinates, so each label is shifted down by 88 to be 1-indexed against this 225-residue construct - A214V is written A126V, and the parent-relative A156V of the scan is written A68V. That numbering is confirmed independently by the paper's catalytically dead control, D154N/H277N, which it calls "equivalent to D145N and H268N of UNG1", UNG1 running exactly 9 residues behind UNG2. The nCas9 nickase the UNG moiety is fused to is not included in the sequence. This file merges two panels run on the same gTBEv0.3 background: the alanine/valine scan of Supplementary Fig. 4a, covering I150-L179 and L210-T217 (38 variants), and the site-saturation scan at position 214 of Supplementary Fig. 4b (19 variants). The two were run on separate plates - their shared gTBEv0.3 control reads 14.47% and 11.07% EGFP+ - so each block is rebased on its own control and the readout is a fold change, which is also how the paper itself quotes these numbers. A214V is the one variant present in both panels and provides the only check on the merge: it rebases to 2.680 in Supplementary Fig. 4a and 3.093 in Supplementary Fig. 4b, about 15% apart; the 4a value is the one kept, since it appears first. Phase 7: the paper states that gTBEv1.1 (v0.3 with A214V) elevates T-to-G conversion "by 2.68-fold" and that gTBEv1.2 (v0.3 with A214T) is elevated "by 1.06-fold in comparison with gTBEv1.1"; rebasing within each panel reproduces both exactly, 2.680 and 1.063, which is what fixes the per-panel basis. Not included as separate work items: the scans on the gTBEv2 background (Supplementary Fig. 5, 10 variants) and the Q259 region scan (Supplementary Fig. 4c), which are different parents and below the 20-variant floor; the cumulative editor versions v1.1 through v5, which are multi-mutation combinations reported only against endogenous sites; and the endogenous-site deep-sequencing editing efficiencies, purity and indel rates of Figs. 3, 6 and Supplementary Figs. 6-18, which cover a handful of editor versions rather than a variant series.

protein: BlaC, Ambler class A broad-spectrum beta-lactamase
source_organism: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (UniProt P9WKD3, full-length precursor including its signal peptide), expressed in Escherichia coli
readout: Relative fitness effect in the presence of carbenicillin and clavulanic acid at 30 C, log of the selected/unselected read-count ratio referenced to wild type, so that wild type is 0 by definition and higher is more resistant
assay_method: Growth selection of a plasmid-borne double-site saturation library in E. coli. Cultures were grown to OD600 = 0.01 in non-selective medium (LB, 50 ug/ml kanamycin) and in selective medium (LB, 50 ug/ml kanamycin, 100 ug/ml carbenicillin, 1 ug/ml clavulanic acid), incubated for 4 h at 30 C, then chilled. Harvested plasmid libraries were amplicon-sequenced on Illumina 150 or 300 bp paired-end platforms, and each variant's relative fitness effect taken as the log of the ratio of its selected to its unselected read counts, referenced to the wild-type ratio, and averaged over two independent trials.
remark: This dataset is library 1 (positions 105 and 130) at 30 C, 20 x 20 saturation of the two sites including wild type at each. Readout is the "Double mutant fitness" column of the "Epi LIB" sheet of Supplementary Data, used as it stands; higher is already better, and the wild-type row is 0 because the fitness is defined relative to it. Sequence is UniProt P9WKD3, the full 307-residue BlaC precursor, fetched whole. The paper numbers residues in the standard Ambler class A scheme, which is not sequential in BlaC, so positions here are the sequential index in this sequence: Ambler 105 -> 117 (Ile), 130 -> 142 (Ser), 132 -> 144 (Gly), 220 -> 236 (Arg), 234 -> 250 (Lys). The map was established by aligning the observed residues of PDB 2GDN (chain A, author numbering = Ambler) onto P9WKD3 in windows around each position, each window matching uniquely; it is corroborated by Ser70 of the catalytic motif landing on index 84 and by the KTG motif reading exactly KTG at 250-252. The offset is not constant (+12, +12, +12, +16, +16 at the five positions), which is why each was mapped separately. The four double-site libraries are NOT merged. Each pairs position 105 with one second site, so the twenty variants carrying wild type at the second site are the same 105 single mutants in all four; those overlaps disagree by a median of 0.22 (37 C) and 0.50 (30 C) fitness units and by as much as 0.66 and 1.17, against a within-library standard deviation of 0.38-0.69 and a reported per-variant error of 0.03-0.08. That spread is too large to treat the libraries as one series, so each library at each temperature is its own dataset, which is also how the paper presents them. Phase 7: the four libraries hold 1,540 distinct genotypes in total and 1,534 of them carry a value at both temperatures, exactly the "1534/1540 (99.6%)" the abstract states. Separately, the deposited Epistasis column equals double-mutant fitness minus the sum of the two single-mutant fitnesses to the last bit (max deviation 0) across all 3,186 rows, confirming that the fitness column read out here is the one the paper's own epistasis analysis used. Not included: the Seq sheets' raw selected/unselected read counts and per-trial fitness, which are the inputs to the averaged fitness used here; and the Epistasis and Significance columns, which are derived from the same fitness values rather than separately measured.

protein: gp44, the ATPase subunit of the bacteriophage T4 sliding-clamp loader, carrying the DEAD-box mutation D110C; four copies of gp44 form subunits B-E of the clamp-loader pentamer
source_organism: Enterobacteria phage T4 (UniProt P04526), expressed from a helper plasmid in Escherichia coli
readout: Fitness (enrichment) value = log10(phage count / library count) for the variant minus the same quantity for the D110C reference allele; higher means the mutation better rescues phage propagation
assay_method: Bacteriophage complementation with deep sequencing. A T4del phage lacking the replication genes of interest is propagated only when the missing proteins are supplied from a helper plasmid; a library of helper plasmids, each carrying one gp44 variant on the D110C background, was transformed into E. coli and the phage released after lysis were sequenced alongside the input plasmid library. A variant's fitness is log10(phage count / library count) for that variant minus the same quantity for the reference allele, so the reference reads 0. Values are averaged over two independent trials (separate transformations), each with two to three replicate infections. The library was built as two pools covering residues 2-115 and 117-230.
remark: The wild-type sequence here is the assayed parent, not the natural protein: it is UniProt P04526 (gp44, 319 aa) with D110C applied, because the whole scan was performed on that DEAD-box background and every fitness value is referenced to it. Mutant codes are therefore written against the D110C parent, so the revertant to the natural aspartate appears as C110D (fitness 0.642, the strongest single rescue at that position). The label check passes with bad = 0: the wild-type residue row of both Fig. 2 final matrices matches P04526 at all 228 scanned positions. Readout is the Fig2_PoolA_finalmatrix and Fig2_PoolB_finalmatrix sheets of Source Data Fig. 2, used as it stands; higher is already better. The two pools cover disjoint position ranges (2-115 and 117-230) and share no variant, so the merge rests on both pools being normalised against the same D110C reference allele rather than on any overlap; position 1, position 116 (a primer-annealing region the paper marks as "no data") and residues 231-319 carry no measurements. protein: XBB.1.5 spike, the SARS-CoV-2 surface glycoprotein, as a cytoplasmic-tail-truncated construct displayed on lentiviral pseudovirus
source_organism: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, XBB.1.5 lineage; libraries produced in 293T cells and assayed on 293T-ACE2 cells
readout: Effect of the mutation on spike-mediated cell entry, log scale relative to the unmutated XBB.1.5 spike; higher means better entry
assay_method: Pseudovirus deep mutational scanning. Barcoded lentiviral libraries of spike variants were used to make spike-pseudotyped virions carrying their own barcoded genome, so a variant's identity is read out by sequencing the barcode. Two independent libraries were made for each spike and all measurements performed in both. Titres of variant pseudovirus on 293T-ACE2 cells relative to the parent, on a log scale; this is the "spike mediated entry" column of the repository's results/summaries/summary.csv.
remark: Sequence is the assayed XBB.1.5 spike construct, 1,249 residues: the spike codon sequence the repository deposits as data/XBB_1_5_spike_codon.fa (GenBank OQ983940.1) translated and truncated to the 1,249 sites its site_numbering_map.csv covers, which is the cytoplasmic-tail-truncated spike used for pseudovirus. One residue was taken from the data rather than that fasta: at reference site 490 (sequential 486) both the full-spike and the RBD-only summary tables give the wild type as F and score S as a mutation with non-zero effects, while the fasta has S; this file follows the tables, since every mutation label is written against them, and records the disagreement here. Readout is the "spike_entry" phenotype of the XBB.1.5 full-spike library summary table, used as it stands; higher is already better, and the WT row is 0 because every phenotype is expressed relative to the unmutated parent. The summary table carries one row per site where mutant equals wild type, with every phenotype exactly 0; those are the parent, not variants, and are collapsed into the single WT row here. Rows with an empty cell in this phenotype are dropped, which is why the three XBB.1.5 full-spike datasets have different variant counts from the same table. The libraries also carry single-residue deletions at key NTD and RBD sites - 289 rows in the XBB.1.5 full-spike table, 108 in the BA.2 table and 27 in the RBD table - which cannot be written as {WT}{pos}{MUT} and are excluded. Phase 7: the summary table's "human sera escape" column is the mean over the ten human sera, and for the 5,239 mutations measured against all ten it equals the mean of the per-serum values in the independently deposited results/summaries/per_antibody_escape.csv to within the files' rounding (median absolute difference 3.0e-06, maximum 4.9e-04). Ranking sites by total positive sera escape puts 473, 357, 420 and 456 first, second, third and fourth of 1,235 sites, matching four of the five the paper names as "the strongest serum escape mutations ... at sites 357, 420, 440, 456 and 473"; the fifth, 440, ranks eighth. Not included: the per-serum escape values in per_antibody_escape.csv, which would be ten more datasets of the same measurement split by donor; the mass-photometry ACE2-occupancy titrations and pseudovirus neutralization validations of Figs. 3 and 4, which cover a few dozen individually built mutants; and the clade-growth modelling of Fig. 5, which is not a per-variant measurement.

protein: TP53, cellular tumour antigen p53
source_organism: Homo sapiens (UniProt P04637), variants installed at the endogenous locus in A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells
readout: Median log2 fold change in pegRNA abundance between day 34 and day 4 under Nutlin-3, over the sensor-filtered pegRNAs encoding the variant; higher means the variant confers more resistance to MDM2 inhibition, that is, more loss of p53 function
assay_method: Prime editing sensor screen. Each epegRNA is paired in the same construct with a synthetic copy of its own endogenous target site (the "sensor"), so the editing rate a pegRNA achieves can be read out from the sensor by amplicon sequencing while its abundance reports the phenotype. A 28,219-member epegRNA library covering TP53 variants was delivered to PEmax-expressing A549 cells; pegRNA abundance was sequenced at day 4 and day 34 in triplicate under continuous Nutlin-3 treatment, which selects for loss of p53 function, and log2 fold changes computed with MAGeCK.
remark: Sequence is UniProt P04637 (human p53, 393 aa) fetched whole; the label check passes with bad = 0 across all 759 distinct missense variants the library encodes. Readout is DERIVED, not a column of the deposit. The screen publishes MAGeCK log2 fold changes per pegRNA, not per variant, so this file takes the median LFC over the pegRNAs encoding each variant, keeping only pegRNAs whose paired sensor site shows at least 10% correct editing over at least ten aligned sensor reads - the exact filter the Fig. 3c caption states ("LFC of each pegRNA >=10% editing with at least ten sensor reads at D34 relative to D4"). The sensor tables in crispresso_replicates_merged/ carry no pegRNA identifier; they are row-aligned to p53_PE_sensor_FINAL_clean.csv, both files holding exactly 28,219 rows, and are joined on that index. Only missense single-nucleotide variants are written: the library also encodes 4,838 frameshift, 2,104 nonsense, 2,065 silent and 1,051 other pegRNA designs, plus 3,211 deletions, 2,678 insertions and 334 multi-nucleotide variants, none of which can be written as {WT}{pos}{MUT} - and the insertion I254_I255insH, which the paper names as its top hit, is among them. There is no WT row: the library's 327 WT-targeting pegRNAs have no "correct edit" for the sensor to score, so the sensor filter removes them all; wt_readout is therefore empty and the z-score is anchored on the dataset mean. The paper focuses its analyses on this treatment arm, "because Nutlin-3 treatment selects for loss-of-function TP53 mutations". Phase 7, run on the full sensor-filtered variant set (402 variants, all classes, Nutlin-3 arm) so that the paper's named indels are included: the insertion of a histidine between residues 254 and 255, which the paper calls "the top hit", comes out ranked 1; R196P, N345S and A347P, the other variants the paper names as top enrichers, rank 21, 10 and 20; and R175H, of which the paper says "the most commonly observed TP53 mutation in human cancer, R175H, did not show strong enrichment despite the existence of several R175H pegRNAs exhibiting >=10% editing efficiency", ranks 350 of 402 with a median LFC of -1.24. The hotspots the paper reports as outcompeted, Y220C and G245S, rank 272 and 216, and R248G (rank 7) beats R248Q (rank 224) as the paper describes. One claim does not reproduce: the paper states that at codon 248 "R248Q and R248W were outcompeted by the rarer substitutions R248P and R248G", whereas this aggregation puts R248W at rank 2 and R248P at rank 222. Not included: the untreated and Nutlin-3 arms at days 16 and 25, which are earlier timepoints of the same two selections; the raw per-pegRNA MAGeCK output, which is the input to the aggregation above; the endogenous-locus amplicon sequencing of Fig. 4, which covers a subset of pegRNAs; and the arrayed competition assays of Figs. 5 and 6, which cover about a dozen variants.

source_organism: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, Omicron BA.1 lineage; libraries produced in 293T cells and assayed on 293T-ACE2 cells

Positions are the sequential index of that construct, converted from the reference numbering the escape table uses (the BA.1 map carries insertion codes such as 214a, so the two numberings are not related by a constant offset). Readout is the escape_mean column of results/antibody_escape/2130-1-0114-112_avg.csv, used as it stands; higher is already better in the sense that the readout measures escape from the antibody, following the convention of the other antibody-escape datasets here. There is no WT row: the escape table carries no row where the mutant equals the wild type, escape being defined as zero for the parent; wt_readout is left empty and the z-score is anchored on the dataset mean. Phase 7: the paper states that "mutations at RBD positions R346 and L452 are sites of substantial escape from both antibodies" and that "both antibodies lose potency with mutations at site K444"; ranking sites by total positive escape puts 346, 444 and 452 in the top five of about a thousand sites in all four of this paper's datasets. Sharper still, the paper states that "the reversion mutation S446G in the BA.1 background increases the neutralization potency of both antibodies (negative escape values in heatmaps)": in the BA.1 files here the wild type at reference site 446 is indeed S, and S446G reads -1.608 against COV2-2130 and -1.039 against 2130-1-0114-112, the only strongly negative values at that site; in the BA.2 files the wild type at 446 is G, matching the paper's remark that BA.2 "carries G446". Not included: the per-replicate escape tables (results/antibody_escape/*_rep.csv), which are the inputs to the averages used here; the prob_escape selection tables; and the mouse viral-titre source data of Fig. 4, which compares three antibodies rather than variants.

protein: IscB.m16, a miniature RNA-guided IscB nuclease from a metagenome-derived IscB-omegaRNA system
source_organism: uncultured bacterium, metagenomic assembly; assayed in human HEK293T cells
readout: Editing activity as a percentage of the wild-type IscB.m16 measured in the same screening block, from an EGFP-activation reporter (EGFP+ cells as a fraction of BFP+ mCherry+ cells); higher means more editing
assay_method: Fluorescent GFxxFP reporter assay in HEK293T cells. A disrupted EGFP reporter carrying a target site with an AAAGAA target-adjacent motif is restored by IscB-mediated cleavage and repair, so the fraction of EGFP-positive cells among transfected (BFP+ mCherry+) cells reports the nuclease's editing activity. Two screening blocks were run: an arginine scan across the P1D, TID and RuvC domains, and site-saturation mutagenesis at 18 positions implicated in target-adjacent-motif recognition.
remark: Sequence is the IscB.m16 amino acid sequence quoted verbatim from Supplementary Table 1, 513 aa; the label check passes with bad = 0 across all 395 variants. Readout is DERIVED: the two source blocks were measured on different plates and their wild-type controls differ two-fold (39.63% in Source Data Fig. 3a, 20.70% in Source Data Fig. 3b), so each block was rebased on its own wild type and the readout is the percentage of that block's wild-type activity, which makes the WT row exactly 100. The two blocks share no variant at all - the arginine scan mutates one set of positions to R, the saturation scan saturates a different 18 - so this merge rests entirely on the wild-type control meaning the same thing in both blocks; that is an assumption, not something the data verifies. 137 variants come from the arginine scan (the table lists 138, one of which, N168R, carries no value) and 258 from the saturation scan; there are no duplicate genotypes between them. Phase 7 was run per block, before rebasing. Block 3a: the paper states that "over 20 of 138 variants in the RuvC domain exhibited improved editing activity compared to wild-type (WT) IscB, with one variant (E326R) showing the highest editing activity" - this file gives 29 variants above wild type, and E326R is the maximum at 47.53%. Block 3b: the paper states that "some variants, especially P460S, T462H, T462L and T465V, greatly enhanced the editing activity" - those four rank 1, 2, 3 and 7 of 258. Not included: the target-adjacent-motif pool screens of Fig. 3d and the omegaRNA scaffold variants of Fig. 2 and Supplementary Table 4, which vary the guide RNA rather than the protein; the base-editor activity data of Figs. 4 and 5, which compare a handful of finished constructs; and the off-target predictions of Supplementary Tables 6-15, which are computational.
